title: The Superconducting Talbot Effect in Phased-Array Josephson Junctions
abstract: We introduce the superconducting Talbot effect---a macroscopic quantum self-imaging phenomenon occurring when proximitized Cooper pairs propagate through a ballistic two-dimensional electron gas. By configuring periodic superconducting leads into a phased-array Josephson junction with programmable phase differences, we demonstrate active steering of the resulting superconducting Talbot carpet. To overcome transport resolution limits, we design a Vernier-scale collector array that performs sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern. This approach maps real-space quantum interference with high robustness to disorder, enabling direct extraction of Fermi wavelengths across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split Fermi surfaces. Tight-binding numerical calculations on a square lattice validate the real-space interference patterns. Our results establish a versatile framework for coherent wavefront engineering and quantum materials diagnostics in superconducting optics.
summary: This paper demonstrates the superconducting Talbot effect in phased-array Josephson junctions to probe the electronic structure of 2DEGs. By actively controlling the junction phase and using sub-wavelength sampling, the authors can measure the lateral shift of the quantum interference pattern. This technique provides a versatile method for directly extracting Fermi wavelengths and characterizing complex Fermi surface textures.
main_problem: The paper investigates the superconducting Talbot effect, a macroscopic quantum self-imaging phenomenon, and develops a method to extract fundamental Fermi wavelengths from this effect.
main_result: The superconducting Talbot effect is successfully demonstrated using phased-array Josephson junctions, allowing for the active steering and measurement of the underlying Fermi wavelength across various Fermi surface types.
method: The authors use a phased-array Josephson junction (PAJJ) coupled with a Vernier-scale collector array to perform sub-wavelength sampling of the fractional Talbot pattern.
model_or_system: The physical system is a proximitized two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) interfaced with a PAJJ. The analysis employs tight-binding models on a square lattice and utilizes the Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian to describe the induced superconducting order parameter.
key_observables: The lateral shift ($\Delta x(L)$) of the fractional Talbot pattern peak position, and the phase-dependent critical current ($I_c$) as a function of the applied phase difference ($\Delta\phi$).
important_parameters: Fermi wavelength ($\lambda_p$), phase difference ($\Delta\phi$), and the Talbot distance ($Z_T$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the ability to map real-space quantum interference patterns and assumes the applicability of the tight-binding model to describe the superconducting gap.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the superconducting Talbot effect, the dependence of critical current on pair wavelength for different Fermi surfaces, and the use of a regression model to fit the phase-dependent critical currents to diagnose Fermi surface textures.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the superconducting Talbot effect and its measurement via critical current oscillations. It then details the advanced technique using a PAJJ and Vernier array to measure the lateral shift. Finally, it applies this method to diagnose the Fermi surface texture across helical, spin-degenerate, and spin-orbit-split regimes.
why_interesting: This work bridges concepts from quantum optics (Talbot effect) and condensed matter physics (superconductivity, Fermi surfaces) using superconducting Josephson junctions, providing a novel, non-destructive diagnostic tool for quantum materials.
